lessons.title: Payables Work Areas and the Invoice Lifecycle

slots.practicalActivity: In your Oracle Fusion practice environment, open the Payables work area and click through each of its sub-tabs (Invoices, Payments, Suppliers-related links) without entering anything yet, writing down which real screen you'd land on for each of the four invoice statuses (Incomplete, Validated, Approved, Paid) the lesson described. Then sketch the procure-to-pay chain on paper -- requisition to PO to receipt to invoice to payment -- and mark with an X exactly where Payables' own responsibility starts and stops.
slots.deliverable: A written map of the Payables work area's navigation paths to each invoice status, plus a hand-drawn procure-to-pay diagram marking Payables' scope.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment's Setup and Maintenance work area, locate the Manage Payables Options task for your business unit and record the actual invoice tolerance values and discount settings you find configured there. Then open Manage Payment Terms, inspect an existing Net 30 term, and build your own new payment term named "Net 15 2% 10" that offers a 2% discount if paid within 10 days, otherwise due in 15.
slots.deliverable: A written record of your BU's real Payables Options tolerance settings, plus a newly created "Net 15 2% 10" payment term saved in the practice environment.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Payables Fundamentals: using the seven-area setup map from Lesson 3 (BU/ledger, Payables/System Options, payment terms, tax, suppliers, bank accounts/payment methods, approval rules), write a one-line diagnosis for each of these four symptoms, naming the exact setup area responsible: (1) an invoice is stuck on a price-variance hold, (2) an invoice has no due date, (3) an invoice needs a manager's sign-off, (4) a new vendor can't be paid yet. Then verify each diagnosis by locating the matching task in the practice environment's Setup and Maintenance work area.
slots.deliverable: A four-symptom diagnostic worksheet matching each problem to its correct Payables setup area, verified against real task names in Setup and Maintenance.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment's Suppliers work area, create a new supplier named "Hearthstone Logistics" (the fictional vendor from Lesson 7) as Spend Authorized with a US tax country and a tax registration number, add one address named "Hearthstone HQ," and build one site named "Hearthstone Pay Site" from that address. Stop before assigning a business unit to the site and write down, from memory, which later lessons (addresses/classifications, bank account, qualification) still need to be completed before this supplier can actually be paid.
slots.deliverable: A real supplier record "Hearthstone Logistics" created in the practice environment with one address and one site, plus a written list of what's still missing before it can be paid.

slots.practicalActivity: Continuing the Hearthstone Logistics supplier record from the previous slot, add a second address for a remittance location, record a business classification (for example small business or minority-owned) on the Business Classifications tab, and attach a bank account on the Payments tab with a routing and account number you invent for practice purposes only. Confirm the "Hearthstone Pay Site" now shows a usable payment method tied to that bank account.
slots.deliverable: The Hearthstone Logistics supplier record updated with a second address, one business classification, and an attached bank account on its pay site.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment, change Hearthstone Logistics' business relationship from Prospective to Spend Authorized if it isn't already, and write down in your own words the qualification checkpoints a Prospective supplier would normally clear first. Then create a second, deliberately near-duplicate supplier record ("Hearthstone Logistics Inc.") and use the supplier merge task to combine it into the original, verifying only one active record remains afterward.
slots.deliverable: A written qualification checklist for moving a supplier from Prospective to Spend Authorized, plus a completed supplier-merge exercise leaving one clean active record.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Suppliers: build one complete, usable supplier record from scratch in the practice environment, end to end -- name, Spend Authorized relationship, tax registration, at least one address, one site assigned to your business unit, one business classification, and one bank account on the Payments tab -- without reusing Hearthstone Logistics. Take a screenshot (or written log) of each tab once it's filled in, to prove the record is actually invoice-ready, not just saved.
slots.deliverable: A brand-new, fully invoice-ready supplier record built independently in the practice environment, documented tab by tab.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment, create a standard, non-PO invoice from the supplier you built in the lab, using an invoice number you invent (matching the lesson's point that the number represents the supplier's own bill, not a system sequence), an invoice date, and an amount of your choosing. Save it, then immediately try entering the exact same invoice number again for the same supplier to see Payables' duplicate-invoice warning fire, and write down exactly what message appears.
slots.deliverable: One saved standard invoice in the practice environment, plus a written record of the duplicate-invoice warning triggered by re-entering its invoice number.

slots.practicalActivity: On the invoice saved in the previous slot, add two or three invoice lines whose amounts sum exactly to the invoice header total, and review the distribution each line generates on the Distributions tab. Then create a reusable distribution set in Setup and Maintenance that splits any invoice amount 70/30 across two GL accounts, and apply it to a second practice invoice to confirm the distributions populate automatically.
slots.deliverable: A multi-line invoice whose lines reconcile to its header total, plus a new 70/30 distribution set applied successfully to a second invoice.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short process memo (no coding required) describing, step by step, how an invoice staged for import by a supplier EDI feed moves through the Payables Open Interface into a real invoice, including what happens to a record that fails import validation. Then, on a new practice invoice, add a tax line manually and compare it against a second invoice where you let Payables' tax engine calculate the tax automatically, noting any difference in the resulting distributions.
slots.deliverable: A written invoice-import process memo covering the failure path, plus a side-by-side comparison of manual versus calculated tax on two practice invoices.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Invoices: in the practice environment, enter three standard invoices for the same supplier in one sitting -- one single-line invoice, one multi-line invoice using the distribution set you built, and one invoice with a manually entered tax line -- and save all three without validating yet (validation is next chapter). Write a short note on which of the three took the least manual data entry, and why.
slots.deliverable: Three saved, unvalidated practice invoices (single-line, distribution-set, manual-tax) with a written comparison of data-entry effort.

slots.practicalActivity: Run Validate on each of the three invoices saved in the previous lab and record the resulting status for each. Deliberately break one invoice -- post a distribution to an inactive GL account -- to trigger a real account hold, confirm it appears on the Manage Holds action, then correct the account and re-validate to watch the hold clear itself automatically, matching Lesson 19's automatic-release category.
slots.deliverable: Validation results for three invoices plus a documented account-hold, correction, and automatic-release cycle on a fourth.

slots.practicalActivity: Submit one of your validated invoices for approval if workflow is enabled in the practice environment, and record each approval status it passes through. Then practice correcting a mistake two different ways on two separate invoices: adjust a line amount on one (an adjustment/correction), and fully cancel the other, writing down which real-world situation would call for each approach rather than the other.
slots.deliverable: A tracked invoice-approval status history, plus one corrected invoice and one cancelled invoice with a written explanation of when to use each method.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Validation, Holds and Approvals: take the Lesson 19 worked example (an invoice from Vantree Industrial Parts with both a matching hold at 7% over tolerance and an account hold on an inactive account) and, in the practice environment, recreate both conditions on one invoice of your own. Resolve the account hold through re-validation, then write a one-paragraph justification for whether you would request a tolerance override or go back to the supplier to correct the matching hold, and why simply clicking Release would not work for it.
slots.deliverable: One practice invoice recreating a dual-hold scenario, with the account hold resolved and a written justification for resolving the matching hold.

slots.practicalActivity: Recreate the Lesson 24 Harbor Point Logistics scenario yourself in the practice environment: enter a PO line for 200 units at a price you choose, log a receipt for only 180 units, then enter and match an invoice billing the full 200. Confirm Payables places a Quantity Received hold, and write down the exact two ways you could clear it (wait for the remaining receipt, or correct the invoice quantity to 180).
slots.deliverable: A recreated PO/receipt/invoice quantity mismatch in the practice environment showing a real Quantity Received hold, with both resolution paths documented.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup and Maintenance, find your business unit's matching tolerance percentages and write down what price and quantity variance they currently allow before a hold fires. Then recreate the Lesson 26 BrightPath Consulting Group example: create and pay a $6,000 prepayment invoice for a 30% deposit on a $20,000 engagement, enter the $20,000 standard invoice when it "arrives," and apply the prepayment so the net amount payable comes to $14,000.
slots.deliverable: A written record of your BU's real matching tolerance settings, plus a completed $6,000 prepayment applied against a $20,000 standard invoice.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment, enter a supplier credit memo for a partial return against one of your earlier invoices, and separately enter a debit memo representing a charge you're billing back to a supplier. Then write a short explanation, in your own words, of how withholding tax and construction retainage both work by holding back part of a payment, and name one concrete difference between the two.
slots.deliverable: One practice credit memo and one debit memo entered against real invoices, plus a written comparison of withholding versus retainage.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Matching and Special Invoices: pick one supplier and run it through the full matching spectrum in the practice environment -- a two-way matched invoice that passes clean, a three-way matched invoice with an intentional receipt shortfall, and a prepayment applied against a later standard invoice for the same supplier. Document the final status of all three and which hold types (if any) you had to resolve.
slots.deliverable: Three documented matching scenarios (two-way, three-way with a resolved hold, and an applied prepayment) for one supplier in the practice environment.

lessons.title: Payment Methods and Payment Process Profiles

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup and Maintenance, review the disbursement bank account configured for your business unit and the payment methods (check, EFT, wire) available on it, writing down which Payment Process Profile each method is tied to. Then open one of your validated practice invoices and confirm which payment method it would default to based on its supplier site, before any payment is actually run.
slots.deliverable: A written inventory of your BU's disbursement bank account, its available payment methods, and the Payment Process Profile each maps to.

slots.practicalActivity: Pay one validated invoice individually using a Quick Payment in the practice environment, noting how fast that path is for a single urgent payment. Then recreate the Lesson 32 Solace Robotics example at smaller scale: validate at least three invoices across two suppliers, run a Payment Process Request selecting them by pay-through date, review the proposed payments, deliberately pull one invoice out of the batch during review, and build the remaining payments.
slots.deliverable: One invoice paid by Quick Payment, plus a completed Payment Process Request with a documented review step where one invoice was removed before building payments.

slots.practicalActivity: Format the Payment Process Request from the previous slot into an electronic payment file and confirm it generated successfully. Then recreate the Lesson 42 Cascade Industrial Parts scenario: pick one issued payment, mark it as needing to be voided (as if the bank never received funds), and walk through the void-and-reissue steps rather than cancelling the underlying invoice or creating a new one.
slots.deliverable: One generated electronic payment file, plus one payment voided and reissued using the correct Payables workflow instead of a new invoice or PO.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment, record a supplier refund scenario where a supplier owes money back (for example, an overpayment on the prepayment you applied earlier) and work through how Payables records that refund as money coming in rather than going out. Write a short comparison of a supplier refund versus a standard credit memo, naming when each is the correct tool.
slots.deliverable: A documented supplier-refund scenario in the practice environment, plus a written comparison of refunds versus credit memos.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Payments: run one supplier's invoice completely through the payment cycle in the practice environment, from validated invoice to a formatted, transmittable electronic payment file, including at least one deliberate void-and-reissue along the way. Write a one-page process narrative documenting every screen you touched, in order, as if training a new AP clerk.
slots.deliverable: A documented end-to-end payment cycle (invoice through electronic payment file, with a void/reissue) and a one-page training narrative.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick three of your practice invoices from earlier chapters (one standard, one matched, one paid) and run Create Accounting in Draft mode first to preview the journal entries without posting, then re-run it in Final mode. Write down each transaction's resulting accounted status and what distinguishes Draft from Final in practice, not just in theory.
slots.deliverable: A written log of three practice transactions run through Create Accounting in both Draft and Final mode, with resulting accounted statuses.

slots.practicalActivity: Transfer the Final-mode journal batches from the previous slot to the General Ledger and confirm they post, walking the accounted-to-transferred-to-posted pipeline end to end on your own data. Then run the Payables Accrual Reconciliation Report and, using the Lesson 39 Meridian Office Supply pattern, write a short note distinguishing a normal timing gap in your results from anything that looks like a stale, uncorrected balance.
slots.deliverable: A posted GL batch traced through the full accounted/transferred/posted pipeline, plus a written accrual-reconciliation analysis distinguishing timing gaps from stale balances.

slots.practicalActivity: Run the Payables aging report in the practice environment and identify which of your own open invoices, if any, fall into each aging bucket. Then work the full seven-step Lesson 41 close checklist against your practice business unit for the current period -- validation complete, holds resolved, payments processed, Create Accounting in Final, GL transfer and post -- and run the Payables-to-Ledger Reconciliation report, recording whether it ties to zero. Finish by working all four Lesson 42 diagnostic scenarios in writing (the Harbor Point unvalidated invoice, the Cascade Industrial Parts payment dispute, the Solace Robotics $2,400 reconciliation gap, and the Meridian Office Supply growing accrual balance), naming the specific chapter and tool that resolves each, then write a two-paragraph course capstone naming the single biggest mistake a brand-new AP clerk would make in their first month and exactly which lesson prevents it.
slots.deliverable: An aging-report snapshot of your own practice invoices, a completed period-close checklist with a Payables-to-Ledger Reconciliation result, written diagnoses for all four course-closing troubleshooting scenarios, and a capstone summary naming the biggest new-AP-clerk mistake and its preventive lesson.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can run the full Oracle Fusion Payables cycle hands-on in the practice environment -- creating and maintaining suppliers, entering and validating invoices, resolving holds, matching against purchase orders and receipts, processing payments, and closing and reconciling a Payables period against the General Ledger.
